assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new door: twisting two graphene sheets to a magic angle produces flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in a single tunable material. The 2018 observations opened moire quantum materials, and the discovery is both experimentally original and conceptually surprising.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery. The three-name configuration is plausible, but the experimental first author (Yuan Cao) and other contributors such as Dean and Young for hBN-encapsulated devices are not on the list, which I would want to check against the record.
assessment.maturity: Insulating and superconducting phases have been reproduced by many independent groups across several moire systems in under a decade. The field is young and the superconducting mechanism is still debated, which makes timing slightly early but defensible.
uncertainties: Credit for the experimental discovery involves junior researchers and other groups not in the credited set.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder are still being addressed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single NV centre spins in diamond gave a room-temperature solid-state quantum system that can be seen, initialised and measured. It is a tool that opened nanoscale sensing, quantum networks and biological measurement, and it has clear instrumental impact.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group reported optical detection of single NV spins in the late 1990s and, with Jelezko, coherent control in 2004. Lukin's later contributions on sensing and spin-register protocols are important but are later developments and in my view more applied than original. I therefore propose the two original experimenters and leave out the third name, though this is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent laboratories over two decades, with commercial and research instrumentation now in use. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the original detection or on the later sensing applications is unsettled.
Early NV work by others may complicate the allocation; I cannot verify details from the longlist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainty far below the caesium standard and enables redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. A genuine invention with verified, quantitative performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2003 and demonstrated early strontium clocks; Ye's group carried the clock to the extreme accuracy and stability that makes it a world standard. Two names fit the record cleanly. Related earlier work on combs and ion clocks has already been honoured separately.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have confirmed and surpassed the original performance; the redefinition of the second is under discussion, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock and comb prizes may be seen as incremental by some members.
Role of other early proposals and groups in lattice-clock history is not fully clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measurement of the last unknown neutrino mixing angle theta-13 by reactor antineutrino disappearance was a clean, decisive experiment. It showed that CP violation in the lepton sector is accessible and it completed the mixing matrix.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) announced a nonzero theta-13 in 2012, with Double Chooz and T2K contributing as well. Three names can cover the leading reactor results, but collaborations of hundreds and a competing experiment make the allocation delicate, and Double Chooz leaders are absent from the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Results were confirmed by independent reactor and accelerator experiments, and precision has kept improving. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K is contested.
Large-collaboration credit to individual spokespeople is a recurring difficulty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Iron-based superconductors were a surprising second family of high-Tc materials beyond the cuprates, opening a large experimental field in materials and spectroscopy. The discovery was experimental and original, in the spirit of the prize, though practical benefit is still emerging.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group reported superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx in 2008, the original discovery. Zhao and Chen's groups rapidly raised Tc above 40 and 55 K with rare-earth substitution. I favour Hosono as the decisive contributor, with a second name for the Tc enhancement, but allocation between Zhao and Chen is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly replicated and developed worldwide. The pairing mechanism remains unresolved and no room-temperature application has emerged, so recognition could be seen as timely or somewhat early.
uncertainties: Fair split between the discovery and the Tc-raising work, and between Zhao and Chen.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions in 1995 made spin-dependent tunnelling practical and underlies hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It has tangible benefit and strong experimental clarity, although it follows the 2007 GMR prize in the same broad topic.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is the original experiment. Parkin's MgO barrier work and later epitaxial devices greatly improved performance and made commercial use feasible, so excluding Parkin is a judgement; Julliere's 1975 low-temperature result is a precursor.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and commercial use. Recognition is mature, perhaps late.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the 1995 discovery or the MgO enhancement.
Julliere's 1975 precursor and the overlap with the earlier GMR prize may weigh against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators, with the HgTe experimental realisation, created a new class of materials with protected edge states. Important and verified, with an experiment confirming a prediction.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original graphene-based prediction and Z2 classification; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe realisation and Konig and Molenkamp observed it in 2007; 3D topological insulators involve Fu, Kane, Mele, Hasan and others. The credited three omit key figures, so the attribution is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed in many materials. The field is mature, but practical applications remain limited.
uncertainties: Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and 3D topological-insulator contributors are not covered.
Possible overlap with B007, which I did not rank.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 opened neutrino astronomy using an instrument built at the South Pole. It is a genuine new window on the universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the driving figure of IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA, but the discovery is the work of a large collaboration, and a prize would probably need to recognise others that the longlist does not credit. The single-name configuration is therefore fragile.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is confirmed by IceCube and other detectors; source identification is still sparse, so the field is maturing but still developing.
uncertainties: Single-person credit may not reflect who did the original work.
Source origin of most neutrinos remains unknown.
Independent confirmation from other detectors is still limited.
